question: Assume today is 2026-10-28. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of cars manufactured in the United Kingdom in September 2026 (total car production for home and export markets, excluding commercial vehicles), as it will be first reported in the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders' (SMMT) monthly UK car manufacturing release.

target.what: Total number of passenger cars manufactured in the United Kingdom during September 2026, for both home and export markets, excluding commercial vehicles, as first reported in SMMT's monthly UK car manufacturing release.
target.publisher: Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT)
target.caveats: Working interpretation is SMMT passenger-car production, not registrations, sales, shipments, or commercial vehicles. The September 2026 period is complete at the cutoff; the SMMT release may not yet be published and any first-reported figure is subject to later revision. If a first-reported SMMT fi

candidates.hypothesis: The most direct route is the target's own recent level and seasonal pattern: September 2026 output should be close to the 2026 year-to-date run-rate adjusted by the historical September effect, including summer-shutdown recovery and working days. Recent monthly totals also reveal whether 2026 is trending up or down. Expected direction is central, but September may be above or below August depending on shutdown timing.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT monthly UK passenger-car production totals for Jan-Aug 2026 (and any Sep 2026 first release dated on/before 2026-10-28), plus September values for 2019-2025 and home/export splits. Minimum needed: at least 2025 September and 2026 monthly year-to-date totals; revisions useful.

candidates.hypothesis: September typically accounts for a stable share of annual output or has a stable ratio to adjacent months in the UK car industry; this share can convert a 2026 annual forecast or August 2026 level into a September estimate. The relationship can be distorted by shutdown timing and model cycles.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical September share of annual UK car production for 2015-2025, September-to-August and September-to-July ratios, working-day counts, and plant holiday/shutdown calendars. Substitute: quarterly SMMT production shares if monthly history is incomplete.
search_hints: UK car production September share annual SMMT
SMMT car manufacturing seasonal August shutdown
UK car output monthly seasonal pattern

candidates.hypothesis: UK passenger-car output is bounded by installed assembly capacity, shift patterns, and September operating days. Summing major plant capacities times utilisation and exposure days gives an independent capacity-based estimate. Transfer assumption: published capacity is nameplate and current utilisation may differ by plant.
candidates.data_to_find: Installed passenger-car capacity by major UK plant (Nissan Sunderland, Toyota Burnaston, BMW Mini Oxford/Swindon, JLR sites, Vauxhall Ellesmere Port, others), current shift patterns, planned September 2026 shutdowns/working days, and average utilisation. Minimum: total UK car capacity and either average utilisation or major plant outputs.
search_hints: UK car plant capacity Nissan Sunderland Toyota Burnaston BMW Oxford 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Plant-specific events in September 2026 such as model changeovers, supply shortages, strikes, energy or demand cuts, and planned maintenance can push output away from run-rate. Confirmed downtime or shift changes should adjust the capacity/run-rate route; direction is event-specific.
candidates.data_to_find: Announcements dated on/before 2026-10-28 from UK car manufacturers and unions about September 2026 temporary shutdowns, shift reductions, model launches/changeovers, supply-chain incidents, and inventory corrections. Minimum: list of major plants with any confirmed September downtime or production-plan changes.

candidates.hypothesis: SMMT or manufacturer forecasts for 2026 UK car production provide an annual or quarterly level that, combined with seasonal shares, constrains September. These are expectations or targets, not realised output, so they should be treated as a prior rather than the answer.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT 2026 UK car production forecast (annual or quarterly), automotive industry outlook published on/before 2026-10-28, and manufacturer production guidance for 2026. Minimum: one 2026 annual forecast with enough detail to apply September seasonality.

candidates.hypothesis: Exports are a large share of UK car production; if recent export share is stable, an export-volume indicator for September 2026 can be divided by that share to estimate total production. HMRC trade data may lag and include re-exports, so the bridge from trade to factory output must be checked.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT home/export production split for recent months, any September 2026 UK car export volume or trade indicator available by 2026-10-28, and HMRC UK passenger-car export data. Minimum: recent export share of production plus one September export indicator or a clear statement that none is available.
search_hints: UK car production home export split 2026

candidates.hypothesis: If SMMT's September 2026 car manufacturing release was published on or before 2026-10-28, the first-reported total is the target; if not, this confirms the cutoff and prevents using post-cutoff figures. Release timing also determines whether any later monthly or quarterly data are unavailable.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT press-release schedule and the September 2026 UK car manufacturing release; date-stamped media copies or SMMT pages. Minimum: publication date and, if present, the headline total; otherwise confirmation that no release exists by cutoff.
search_hints: SMMT car manufacturing September 2026 release date

If not, confirming the scheduled publication date and any pre-28-Oct summary establishes the cutoff and prevents accidental use of post-cutoff revisions.

extra_directions.hypothesis: Normal September/August ratios and September shares of Jan-Aug cumulative from 2022-2024 would replace the wide assumptions a3/a4 and materially narrow the seasonal route; 2025 values are distorted by the JLR stoppage.

p225.role: UK passenger car production January-August 2026 cumulative, cars, used as the 2026 year-to-date level

a4.role: dimensionless ratio of September 2026 car production to the January-August 2026 cumulative, calibrated to normal September seasonality net of the JLR-distorted 2025 base

methods.rationale: Uses actual Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative car output (p225) and an assumption for the September-to-Jan-August seasonal ratio. This route captures the 2026 level without relying on the JLR-distorted September 2025 base. Shared dependency: p225 is SMMT data and a4 is calibrated from SMMT seasonality. Failure mode: abnormal September 2026 shutdown or incomparability in the Jan-Aug cumulative due to shutdown timing.

p61.role: UK total passenger car production in September 2024, cars, a normal pre-JLR September level

a2.role: dimensionless factor adjusting September 2024 car production to September 2026 using the 2024-to-2026 trend in UK car output

methods.rationale: Uses normal September 2024 actual (p61) adjusted by a two-year trend factor to 2026. This avoids the 2025 JLR distortion but assumes September 2026 follows the same relative decline as Jan-Aug 2024 to Jan-Aug 2026. Shared dependency: p61 is SMMT data and a2 is informed by SMMT YTD data. Failure mode: September-specific plant events or model cycles.

p45.role: UK total passenger car production in September 2025, cars, the JLR-stoppage-depressed base

a1.role: dimensionless recovery factor from September 2025 to September 2026 for UK car production

methods.rationale: Uses September 2025 actual (p45) and a recovery factor for the JLR shutdown base. This directly addresses the depressed 2025 September and the likely 2026 rebound. Shared dependency: p45 is SMMT data and a1 is based on SMMT/JLR stoppage evidence. Failure mode: if September 2026 also has a major stoppage or if recovery is weaker or stronger than assumed.

p3.role: UK total passenger car production in August 2026, cars, the latest observed monthly level

a3.role: dimensionless September-to-August car production ratio for a normal post-summer restart

methods.rationale: Uses the latest August 2026 car output (p3) and a normal September/August restart ratio. This captures the current run-rate and expected summer-shutdown recovery. Shared dependency: p3 is SMMT data and a3 is calibrated from historical seasonality. Failure mode: September restart abnormal, or August shutdown timing differs from the historical pattern.

Standard own-history forecast using monthly car production levels and the Jan-Aug 2026 YTD. It provides a model-based baseline, but because September 2025 was distorted by the JLR stoppage, it may understate a normal September rebound; it is kept as one route rather than the sole estimate.

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 car production change factor
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was an exceptionally low 51,090 cars because JLR stopped UK production for five weeks (p89/p90/p593). By 2026, Jan-Aug car output is only -3.9% YoY (p224/p225) and August 2026 was +6.1% YoY (p3), so a recovery over the depressed September 2025 base is likely. A full return to the normal September 2024 level would imply a larger factor, but the 2026 trend is lower; 1.23 is a central recovery factor with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: No major September 2026 UK car plant stoppage comparable to JLR 2025, and September 2026 follows the 2026 YTD trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: Confirmed prolonged September 2026 plant shutdowns or SMMT data showing September 2026 below September 2025.

assumptions.name: September 2024 to September 2026 trend factor
assumptions.rationale: September 2024 was a normal high month at 70,039 cars (p61). The 2026 Jan-Aug car cumulative 472,851 (p225) is lower than the comparable 2024 Jan-Aug cumulative derived from p254 and p61, so a factor below 1 is appropriate. The range allows for September-specific recovery or further decline.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 follows the same relative trend as Jan-Aug 2024 to Jan-Aug 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: September 2026 plant-specific events or model launches make September deviate materially from the two-year YTD trend.

assumptions.name: September/August production ratio
assumptions.rationale: August is a shutdown month and September restarts lines. The 2025 ratio 51,090/38,693 is depressed by the JLR stoppage; normal 2024 September was 70,039, consistent with a ratio around 1.6-1.7 if August 2024 was near 41,000. The August 2026 level is 39,328 (p3), so this ratio converts the latest month into September.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has a normal post-summer restart and no extended shutdown.
assumptions.falsified_by: SMMT or plant evidence of an extended September shutdown or a much weaker restart.

assumptions.name: September production as ratio of Jan-Aug cumulative
assumptions.rationale: September 2024 was a normal high month and its ratio to Jan-Aug 2024 is higher than the JLR-distorted 2025 ratio. A 2026 ratio between the normal and distorted years is plausible; 0.125 uses the actual Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative 472,851 (p225) without relying on the depressed 2025 September base.
assumptions.applies_when: 2026 Jan-Aug cumulative is complete and September has a normal restart.
assumptions.falsified_by: Major September 2026 disruption or a September seasonal share outside the 2024/2025 range.

a4.role: dimensionless ratio of September 2026 car production to January-August 2026 cumulative car production, calibrated to normal September seasonality net of the JLR-distorted 2025 base

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal-share route using the latest observed SMMT-derived 2026 car cumulative and a normal September share. It avoids relying on the distorted September 2025 base. Main failure mode: September 2026 restart timing or model changeovers could shift the normal September share.

p61.role: UK total passenger car production in September 2024, cars, a normal pre-JLR September level

a2.role: dimensionless factor adjusting September 2024 car production to September 2026 using the 2024-to-2026 trend in UK car output

methods.rationale: Uses September 2024 as a clean September baseline, adjusted for the subsequent UK car-production trend. This is robust to the 2025 JLR anomaly but depends on the trend factor transferring to September and on no major plant-specific difference in 2026.

p45.role: UK total passenger car production in September 2025, cars, the JLR-stoppage-depressed base

a1.role: dimensionless recovery factor from September 2025 to September 2026 for UK car production

methods.rationale: Direct recovery route from the depressed September 2025 SMMT level. The JLR stoppage gives a clear reason September 2026 should be above September 2025, while the 2026 YTD weakness limits the recovery factor. Main risk: a new September 2026 disruption or an incomplete JLR/industry restart.

p3.role: UK total passenger car production in August 2026, cars, the latest observed monthly level

a3.role: dimensionless September-to-August car production ratio for a normal post-summer restart

methods.rationale: Uses the latest monthly SMMT car-production level and a normal September restart ratio. August is usually depressed by summer shutdown timing, so September should rebound. Main failure mode: if 2026 shutdown timing differs materially from the historical pattern, the September/August ratio will be wrong.

Own-history monthly route using kept SMMT car-production levels for January 2026, June-August 2026, December 2025, October 2025, September 2025, September 2024, May 2025 and August 2025. It is a direct target-series benchmark, but because September 2025 was JLR-depressed, this route may understate the September 2026 recovery if treated alone.

assumptions.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 car production change factor
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was severely depressed by the JLR five-week stoppage (p89, p738), so September 2026 should recover much of that lost output. The clean September 2024 level p61 is much higher than p45, but 2026 YTD car output is still below 2025 (p224, p225), so a full return to 2024 levels is not assumed. The central factor reflects a substantial but incomplete recovery from the JLR-distorted base.
assumptions.applies_when: No major new UK plant shutdown, model-changeover disruption or supply crisis occurs in September 2026, and JLR and other plants run near normal September patterns.
assumptions.falsified_by: Confirmed September 2026 plant shutdowns, extended summer shutdowns, or model-changeover stoppages that prevent normal restart; alternatively, evidence that September 2026 recovered fully to pre-stoppage 2024 levels.

assumptions.name: September 2024 to September 2026 trend factor
assumptions.rationale: Uses September 2024 p61 as a clean pre-JLR September baseline. UK car output in 2026 remains below 2025 on a YTD basis (p224, p225), and 2025 itself was below 2024, so a downward trend adjustment is warranted. The range allows for model launches and recovery offsetting part of the decline.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2024 is a reasonable normal-month baseline and the 2024-2026 change in UK car production trend transfers to September 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large new model ramp-up, plant capacity expansion, or a structural decline much larger than the 2024-2026 YTD trend.

assumptions.name: September-to-August car production ratio for a normal post-summer restart
assumptions.rationale: August is normally a low month because of summer shutdowns, and September restarts production. The 2025 September/August comparison is distorted downward by the JLR stoppage, while the 2024 relationship implies a stronger normal restart. The central value is a normal post-shutdown rebound ratio.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 has a normal restart after summer shutdowns and is not affected by an unusually early or extended shutdown.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that summer shutdowns were pulled forward into August 2026 in a way that changes the normal September rebound, or that September 2026 has additional plant downtime.

assumptions.name: September car production as a ratio of January-August cumulative car production
assumptions.rationale: Uses the latest observed January-August 2026 cumulative car production p225. The normal 2024 September share of the January-August cumulative is higher, while the 2025 share is depressed by the JLR stoppage. A central value below the normal 2024 share reflects the weaker 2026 YTD trend but allows for September recovery.
assumptions.applies_when: The January-August 2026 cumulative is complete and comparable in scope to monthly SMMT car production, and September 2026 is a broadly normal production month.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of an abnormal September 2026 shutdown, model changeover, or large revision to the January-August 2026 cumulative.

methods.label: m1

p225.role: UK passenger car production January-August 2026 cumulative, cars, used as the 2026 year-to-date level

a4.role: dimensionless ratio of September 2026 car production to January-August 2026 cumulative car production, calibrated to normal September seasonality net of the JLR-distorted 2025 base

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal-share route using the latest observed SMMT-derived 2026 car cumulative and a normal September share. It avoids relying on the distorted September 2025 base. Main failure mode: September 2026 restart timing or model changeovers could shift the normal September share.

methods.label: m2

p61.role: UK total passenger car production in September 2024, cars, a normal pre-JLR September level

a2.role: dimensionless factor adjusting September 2024 car production to September 2026 using the 2024-to-2026 trend in UK car output

methods.rationale: Uses September 2024 as a clean September baseline, adjusted for the subsequent UK car-production trend. This is robust to the 2025 JLR anomaly but depends on the trend factor transferring to September and on no major plant-specific difference in 2026.

methods.label: m3

p45.role: UK total passenger car production in September 2025, cars, the JLR-stoppage-depressed base

a1.role: dimensionless recovery factor from September 2025 to September 2026 for UK car production

methods.rationale: Direct recovery route from the depressed September 2025 SMMT level. The JLR stoppage gives a clear reason September 2026 should be above September 2025, while the 2026 YTD weakness limits the recovery factor. Main risk: a new September 2026 disruption or an incomplete JLR/industry restart.

methods.label: m4

p3.role: UK total passenger car production in August 2026, cars, the latest observed monthly level

a3.role: dimensionless September-to-August car production ratio for a normal post-summer restart

methods.rationale: Uses the latest monthly SMMT car-production level and a normal September restart ratio. August is usually depressed by summer shutdown timing, so September should rebound. Main failure mode: if 2026 shutdown timing differs materially from the historical pattern, the September/August ratio will be wrong.

methods.label: m5
methods.rationale: Own-history monthly route using kept SMMT car-production levels for January 2026, June-August 2026, December 2025, October 2025, September 2025, September 2024, May 2025 and August 2025. It is a direct target-series benchmark, but because September 2025 was JLR-depressed, this route may understate the September 2026 recovery if treated alone.

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 car production change factor
kept.rationale: September 2025 was severely depressed by the JLR five-week stoppage (p89, p738), so September 2026 should recover much of that lost output. The clean September 2024 level p61 is much higher than p45, but 2026 YTD car output is still below 2025 (p224, p225), so a full return to 2024 levels is not ass
kept.applies_when: No major new UK plant shutdown, model-changeover disruption or supply crisis occurs in September 2026, and JLR and other plants run near normal September patterns.
kept.falsified_by: Confirmed September 2026 plant shutdowns, extended summer shutdowns, or model-changeover stoppages that prevent normal restart; alternatively, evidence that September 2026 recovered fully to pre-stoppage 2024 levels.

kept.name: September 2024 to September 2026 trend factor
kept.rationale: Uses September 2024 p61 as a clean pre-JLR September baseline. UK car output in 2026 remains below 2025 on a YTD basis (p224, p225), and 2025 itself was below 2024, so a downward trend adjustment is warranted. The range allows for model launches and recovery offsetting part of the decline.
kept.applies_when: September 2024 is a reasonable normal-month baseline and the 2024-2026 change in UK car production trend transfers to September 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a large new model ramp-up, plant capacity expansion, or a structural decline much larger than the 2024-2026 YTD trend.

kept.name: September-to-August car production ratio for a normal post-summer restart
kept.rationale: August is normally a low month because of summer shutdowns, and September restarts production. The 2025 September/August comparison is distorted downward by the JLR stoppage, while the 2024 relationship implies a stronger normal restart. The central value is a normal post-shutdown rebound ratio.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 has a normal restart after summer shutdowns and is not affected by an unusually early or extended shutdown.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
